sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Ewing Township different?
sections.html:
Every home sold in Ewing has to pass a township housing inspection first. In a fast sale, the real question is how quickly the property can clear that check. After that, the process is the usual New Jersey deed, transfer fee and tax filings.

Ewing is in Mercer County on the Delaware River, just north and west of Trenton. It covers about 15.6 square miles. The 2020 count was 37,264 residents, the most the township has ever recorded, and the 2025 estimate is 39,030, up 4.5 percent. Blocks near the Trenton line feel urban, while most of the township is residential subdivisions built in separate phases, so house styles change from one neighborhood to the next.

Neighborhood names show up in listings and appraisals, so use the local one: Ewingville, West Trenton, Prospect Heights, Fernwood, Hillwood Lakes, Parkway Village, Scudders Falls or Wilburtha.

Ewing prices sit below the national median value, and a third of households rent. These are 2020 to 2024 estimates.

sections.h2: Roads and rail near Ewing homes
sections.html:
Four major roads cross the township, and the West Trenton rail terminal anchors the commuter side. Interstate 295 clips the northwest corner, Route 29 follows the Delaware River as the Delaware River Scenic Byway, U.S. Route 206 skirts the southeast, and Route 31 (Pennington Road) heads north to Pennington and Flemington.

West Trenton station is the end of SEPTA's West Trenton Line, which mainly carries riders to Philadelphia. NJ Transit buses 601, 607, 608, 609 and 624 connect the township with Trenton, and Trenton-Mercer Airport sits inside the borders.

The Delaware and Raritan Canal runs near the river, and the land along it is part of the Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park. Homes along River Road and Route 29 are close to the water, so check flood-zone status with the township before you quote a price to a buyer who asks.

Ewing gets a lot of rain, which is why the housing inspector looks closely at grading and drainage, roofs, gutters and foundation walls. A downspout that empties against the foundation is cheap to fix and removes an easy objection before the inspector arrives.

sections.h2: What does Ewing's resale inspection check?
sections.html:
Every dwelling or commercial building offered for resale must be inspected and approved by the Ewing Division of Housing. The residential fee on the township's 2025 form is $125. The inspector works from the International Property Maintenance Code and township ordinances. You can request an inspection through the township's SDL portal, which needs an account, or through the Construction Office at 1666 Pennington Road, 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

The printed checklist is not limited to these items, but they come up often:

  • Smoke alarms on every level, using ten-year sealed lithium battery single-station units, and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • A portable fire extinguisher rated at least 2A-10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted no higher than 5 feet, and tagged or receipted within the last 12 months.
  • Ground-fault outlets in kitchens, baths and outdoors, and at least two receptacles per bedroom.
  • Sound handrails, stairs, roofs, windows with screens, and working heating equipment.
  • No double-keyed deadbolts, which the form calls illegal.
  • All open permits closed out, and a well water certificate where a well serves the house.

Some repairs may need Uniform Construction Code permits, so call the office before you hire a contractor.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house in Ewing
sections.html:
Rentals carry extra paperwork here, so settle the registration status before a sale. Under township ordinance 10-07, residential rentals must be registered every year regardless of tenant changes. The registration and rental fire prevention forms are due January 31. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection whenever a tenant changes.

If you sell a rental, hand the buyer the registration record, the latest fire prevention form and any open violation notices. A buyer who plans to live in the house will need the unit vacated on a schedule written into the contract.

sections.h2: Closing costs and recording in Ewing
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee, and the deed is recorded with the Mercer County Clerk in Trenton, whose office has kept property records since 1838. For total consideration of $350,000 or less, the state schedule runs $2.00 per $500 up to $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $3.90 per $500 from $200,000 to $350,000. Ask the closing attorney for the final figure.

The county charges $43 for the first page of a regular deed and $10 for each additional page. The transfer fee can be paid by cash, cashier's check, money order, attorney trust account or business escrow account, and amounts over $10,000 must be certified or bank check. On sales of $1 million and above, the transfer fee often called the mansion tax changed on July 10, 2025 so that the seller pays it.

New Jersey residents sign a GIT/REP-3 at closing. A nonresident owner owes an estimated payment of at least 2 percent of the price unless an exemption applies.

sections.h2: Steps for a quick sale in Ewing
sections.html:
Start with the inspection, because it sets your timeline. Request it through the portal or the Construction Office, and ask what the inspector will look at in your house. Fix the cheap items yourself: alarms, the extinguisher, outlets and handrails. Close out any open permits and, if a well serves the house, get the well water certificate.

Once the Division of Housing approves the property, your closing attorney prepares the deed and the transfer fee and GIT/REP filings. Bring the deed, your latest tax bill and a mortgage payoff figure to that first meeting. A cash buyer can take the house as it is, but the township approval and state filings still apply to the sale.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell a house in Ewing?
faqs.a: Yes. The Division of Housing must inspect and approve every dwelling offered for resale. The residential fee on the 2025 form is $125, and requests go through the SDL portal or the Construction Office at 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

faqs.q: What alarms does a Ewing resale inspection require?
faqs.a: Smoke alarms on every level, using ten-year sealed lithium battery single-station units, and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas. You also need a labeled fire extinguisher near the kitchen that is tagged or receipted within 12 months.

faqs.q: How much does the Mercer County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A regular deed costs $43 for the first page and $10 for each added page. The state transfer fee is paid separately at recording and is set by the sale price. The clerk takes cash, cashier's check, money order, attorney trust account or business escrow account for that fee.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before selling it in Ewing?
faqs.a: Registration is yearly under ordinance 10-07, with forms due January 31, so it should already be on file. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection on each tenant change. Bring the paperwork to the sale so the buyer sees a clean record.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ewing house with open permits?
faqs.a: Open permits must be closed out before the house can pass the resale inspection. Call the Construction Office to find out which final inspections are outstanding. Some repairs also need new Uniform Construction Code permits before work begins.
